newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African troops ready for peacekeeping.
newsitem.headline: S.African troops ready for peacekeeping.

text.p: South Africa has trained two battalions for multi-national peacekeeping and would be willing to contribute up to 1,000 men to such an operation, military officials said on Tuesday.
"The two battalions are trained and are ready to participate," army Colonel Jaco van As told a parliamentary committee discussing proposed defence policy.
South Africa, with one of the most modern forces on the continent, was asked last year to contribute to a multinational peacekeeping force for eastern Zaire.
It was never fully deployed but South Africa baulked at sending a military contingent because it said its new force, comprising former enemies from the apartheid war, was not fully integrated.
Brigadier Len le Roux, presenting the proposals to the committee, said the army envisaged contributing mainly infantry to a peacekeeping force.

"The maximum scale that we foresee that it might be necessary to put in, would be at the level of an army battalion group, in the order of 1,000 soldiers supported by medical, engineering...and so on," he said.
"We don't see South Africa putting a division into this type of operation, I don't think we have the capability or the size."
Le Roux said if South Africa was called on to contribute to a peacekeeping force, it would have one battalion ready to go with a second in training ready to rotate.
The defence proposals said South African skills appropriate to peacekeeping included mine-clearing, communications and medical support.
